words.example: Kate dumped the contents of her bag onto the cabin floor.
examples: The customs officer checked the contents of every crate in the cargo hold.
Matt wondered about the contents of the locked trunk in the stateroom.
When the airship tilted, the contents of the galley shelves crashed to the floor.
Before you buy a snack, read the label to learn about its contents.
I have to check the contents of the drink before I drink it.
words.imageAlt: A travel bag with its clothes, book, apple, and compass spilled out.

words.example: A deficiency of vitamin C can make sailors on long voyages very sick.
examples: The doctor said his tiredness came from an iron deficiency.
A plant with a nitrogen deficiency often grows yellow, droopy leaves.
The inspector found a serious deficiency in the ship's safety equipment.
A deficiency of fuel forced the captain to land the airship early.
A vitamin deficiency can make you feel weak and tired.
words.imageAlt: A nearly empty watering can has too little water for four thirsty plants.

words.example: The island below the airship was densely covered with tall trees.
examples: The city is densely populated, so the streets are crowded all day.
Ferns grew densely along the riverbank, hiding the path.
The clouds were packed so densely that the pilot could not see the ocean.
The jungle was so densely tangled that the explorers had to cut their way through.
The crowd at the concert was so densely packed that we could barely move.
words.imageAlt: Trees grow tightly packed together across an island.

words.example: With favorable winds, the airship would reach Sydney in two days.
examples: The captain waited for favorable weather before taking off.
Sunny skies and a light breeze made conditions favorable for a picnic.
The judges gave her science fair poster a favorable review.
A favorable report from the doctor meant he could rejoin the team.
The weather was favorable for flying a kite in the park.
words.imageAlt: Sunny skies and a gentle wind help an airship travel smoothly.

words.definition: a sudden, strong fear that makes it hard to think clearly or act calmly
words.example: When the alarm rang, panic spread through the passengers.
examples: In a panic, Matt grabbed the railing and held on tight.
The crew tried to keep everyone calm and avoid panic during the storm.
She felt a rush of panic when she realized her ticket was gone.
There is no need for panic; just follow the fire drill steps.
words.imageAlt: A frightened passenger reacts suddenly while a calm adult offers help.

words.definition: to shine an image or light outward
words.example: Mr. Long projected the map onto the classroom screen.
examples: The lighthouse projects a bright beam across the dark sea.
We projected the movie onto a white sheet in the backyard.
The flashlight projects a circle of light on the cave wall.
The airship's searchlight projected a beam down through the fog.

words.example: The captain made a reasonable decision to turn back before the storm.
examples: It is reasonable to wear a coat when the air is freezing.
Ten dollars is a reasonable price for a used bike helmet.
Her excuse sounded reasonable, so the teacher let her hand it in late.
Be reasonable and share the computer with your brother.
It's reasonable to ask for more time if the project is difficult.
words.imageAlt: Two children make a fair choice by sharing strawberries equally.

words.definition: when you feel very confused, usually when you are sick
words.example: The injured balloonist was delirious and kept talking about strange winged creatures.
examples: With a high fever, my brother was delirious and didn't know where he was.
The sailor had gone three days without water and was delirious when they found him.
The fans were delirious with joy when their team won the championship.
Matt sat beside the delirious old man and listened to his mumbled words.
words.imageAlt: A feverish child looks confused while a caring adult stays nearby.

words.definition: a small, round window in the side of a ship or aircraft
words.example: Matt looked through the porthole at the ocean far below.
examples: Sunlight streamed through the cabin's porthole in the morning.
Each passenger cabin on the airship has two portholes.
Rain streaked across the portholes as the ship sailed through the storm.
She pressed her nose against the cold glass of the porthole.
words.imageAlt: A child looks at the ocean through a round brass ship window.

words.example: Mary will attempt to open the rusty garden door.
examples: Colin attempted to stand up by himself for the first time.
Every day she attempts a harder puzzle than the day before.
Do not attempt to climb the wall without a ladder.
The robin attempted to pull a worm from the hard ground.
He made an attempt to climb the tall tree.
words.imageAlt: A child tries hard to push open a heavy garden gate.

words.example: In spring, the garden begins to awaken after the long winter.
examples: The robin's song awakened Mary early in the morning.
The smell of pancakes awakens me every Saturday.
Colin was afraid the noise would awaken the whole house.
Fresh air and sunshine slowly awakened Colin's interest in the world.
words.imageAlt: A child wakes up and stretches as morning sunlight enters the room.

words.example: Mary looked at the spoiled boy with contempt.
examples: The bully showed his contempt by laughing at the younger kids.
Colin treated the servants with contempt until he learned to be kind.
She shook her head in contempt at the rude remark.
His voice was full of contempt when he talked about the rival team.
She looked at the broken toy with contempt, thinking it was useless.
words.imageAlt: A child dismisses another child's handmade crown with a scornful expression.

words.example: The rusty fastening on the garden gate would not budge.
examples: Mary felt along the ivy until her fingers found the fastening of the door.
The fastenings on my backpack broke, so my books fell out.
Check that all the fastenings on your life jacket are tight.
The old trunk had a brass fastening shaped like a bird.
The broken fastening on my backpack made it hard to close.
words.imageAlt: A metal latch holds a wooden garden gate closed.

words.example: A mysterious key lay half-buried in the soil.
examples: Late at night, Mary heard mysterious crying down the long hallway.
The locked garden seemed mysterious to everyone in the house.
A mysterious stranger left a note on our front door.
The scientist could not explain the mysterious lights in the sky.
words.imageAlt: A child discovers a puzzling key partly hidden beneath ivy.

words.definition: to be in charge of a meeting or event
words.example: The principal will preside over the awards ceremony.
examples: Mrs. Medlock presided over the servants of the great house.
A judge presides over the courtroom.
The mayor presided at the opening of the new park.
Our class captain presides over every student council meeting.
Our boss presided over the meeting last December.
words.imageAlt: A student leads a small council meeting while classmates listen.

words.example: Dickon had to restrain the excited fox cub.
examples: Mary could hardly restrain her excitement when she found the key.
The nurse restrained Colin from jumping out of bed.
A strong seat belt restrains each passenger during a crash.
He bit his lip to restrain a laugh during the quiet assembly.
The teacher had to restrain the puppy from running out the door.
words.imageAlt: A child holds a leash to keep an excited puppy safely back from the road.

words.example: The robin was the only witness when Mary found the buried key.
examples: Two witnesses saw the gardener lock the gate.
The police officer asked the witness to describe the car.
Ben Weatherstaff was a witness to Colin's first steps in the garden.
The judge listened carefully to each of the witnesses.
The police asked the witness what he saw during the accident.
words.imageAlt: A child watches another child accidentally knock over a flowerpot.

words.definition: tangled together in a thick, messy mass
words.example: The stray dog's fur was matted with mud.
examples: The old rose bushes were matted with dead leaves and vines.
After the storm, her wet hair was matted against her face.
The grass under the melted snow was flat and matted.
Dickon gently brushed the lamb's matted wool.
words.imageAlt: A lamb's wool is tangled into thick messy clumps.

words.definition: a thin, curling stem that a climbing plant uses to wrap around and hold onto things
words.example: Green tendrils of ivy curled around the garden wall.
examples: A pea plant wraps its tendrils around the fence as it grows.
Mary gently pulled a tendril away from the hidden door.
The tendril of the grapevine coiled tightly around the stick.
Thin tendrils reached out from the vine toward the sunlight.
words.imageAlt: A thin curling pea-plant stem wraps around a wooden support.

words.definition: to stop and pause before you do something
words.example: If you need help, don't hesitate to ask.
examples: The poet hesitated before reading her poem aloud to the class.
Mia hesitates every time she has to dive off the high board.
He hesitated at the door, unsure whether to knock.
When the bell rang, no one hesitated to rush outside.
When it was finally his turn to go on stage, Ben didn't hesitate.
words.imageAlt: A child pauses uncertainly before knocking on a classroom door.

words.definition: the part of a song or poem that repeats
words.example: Everyone joined in on the refrain of the song.
examples: The poet repeats the same refrain at the end of every stanza.
A catchy refrain makes a song easy to remember.
Our class poem has two refrains that we read aloud together.
Each time the refrain came back, the audience clapped along.
During his song, the whole audience joined in for the refrain, singing the same catchy line each time it came around.
words.imageAlt: The same golden chorus returns after a different blue verse in a children's song.

words.definition: unable to relax or sit still
words.example: The restless kids wiggled in their seats during the long assembly.
examples: After a week of rainy days, the puppy was restless.
I spent a restless night worrying about the test.
The restless sea tossed the little boat up and down.
The crowd grew restless when the concert started late.
Ben felt restless all week before the talent show, unable to sit still in class because he was so nervous.
words.imageAlt: A child keeps wiggling and tapping instead of sitting still.

words.example: Seize the rope before the boat drifts away!
examples: The eagle seized a fish from the river.
She seizes every chance to read a new poem.
The guards seized the thief by the arm.
Don't wait for luck; seize the moment and try out for the team.
Backstage, his little sister tried to seize his trophy before he even got a chance to hold it!
words.imageAlt: A hand quickly grabs a rope to keep a boat from drifting away.

words.example: The watchful lifeguard spotted the swimmer in trouble.
examples: Under the watchful eye of her coach, Mia practiced her flips.
Stay watchful when you cross a busy street.
The watchful mother bird never left her chicks alone.
A watchful reader notices the small clues in a mystery.
His teacher reminded him to be watchful during rehearsal, looking closely for any mistakes in the dance routine.
words.imageAlt: An alert lifeguard carefully watches children swimming in a pool.

words.definition: to write or draw something quickly and messily
words.example: He scrawled a poem on a paper napkin.
examples: Don't scrawl your answers; write neatly so the teacher can read them.
My little brother scrawls his name on every drawing.
She grabbed a pen to scrawl a quick note before the bus came.
The poet was scrawling new lines in her notebook as fast as she could think.
words.imageAlt: A hand writes hurried, messy pencil marks on a napkin.

words.definition: a short, simple song or poem, often light and cheerful
words.example: Grandma hummed a little ditty while she baked bread.
examples: The class made up a silly ditty about homework.
The ice-cream truck plays the same ditty every afternoon.
My sister made up a funny ditty to help me remember the planets.
He wrote a short ditty for his mom's birthday card.
words.imageAlt: Two children sing a short cheerful tune with a ukulele.
